topicName: Load Balancers, Reverse Proxies, and CDN Behavior
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Load Balancers, Reverse Proxies, and CDN Behavior in Performance Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When conducting performance testing, understanding the underlying network architecture is critical. Load balancers, reverse proxies, and content delivery networks (CDNs) heavily influence how traffic hits your application, how latency is perceived, and where bottlenecks occur."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Reverse Proxies vs. Load Balancers"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A reverse proxy sits in front of one or more web servers, intercepting requests from clients. While reverse proxies (such as NGINX or HAProxy) can handle security, SSL termination, and caching, load balancers specifically focus on distributing incoming network traffic across multiple backend servers to ensure reliability and high availability."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Load Balancing Algorithms"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Round Robin: Distributes requests sequentially across the server pool."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Least Connections: Routes traffic to the server with the fewest active connections, ideal for long-lived sessions."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"IP Hash: Uses the client's IP address to determine which server receives the request, ensuring session persistence."},{"order":9,"type":"heading","text":"2. CDN Behavior and Caching Layers"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"CDNs cache static assets (images, JavaScript, CSS) at Edge servers distributed globally. During a performance test, failing to account for CDN caching can skew your metrics. If your test scripts hammer origin servers for cached assets, you are not simulating realistic user behavior."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Cache-Control Headers Example"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable"},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"3. Performance Testing Implications"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Performance engineers must isolate CDN and load balancer metrics from backend application metrics. Key areas to monitor include:"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cache Hit Ratio (CHR): A low CHR during load tests indicates misconfigured cache headers, forcing excessive origin requests."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"SSL Handshake Latency: Measure the time taken by the reverse proxy to terminate TLS connections."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Connection Pooling and Keep-Alive: Ensure load balancers maintain persistent connections to backend nodes to avoid TCP overhead."},{"order":18,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Incorporating reverse proxies, load balancers, and CDN edge behavior into your test design ensures your performance results closely mirror production realities. Always validate your cache headers and monitor edge node latency independently of your origin servers."}]
